label: the crawler (models/headcrab.mdl): a sludge crawler: low, wet, six-legged, the size of a headcrab, grey-green with a pale belly and a ring of teeth

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/houndeye.mdl, models/chumtoad.mdl, models/roach.mdl: the judge does not know which
measured.contract: keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: Low and six-legged, but the body is two boxy, faceted lobes (sides.png LEFT and TOP) rather than a wet, low dome, and the teeth stick out as a small cluster at the front (FRONT, LEFT, BELOW) rather than the brief's ring. The outline is not the brief's.

M2.reason: The brief gives no number (sizeAsked null, sizeOff null), so nothing was measured against it. By eye the 42-unit length, legs included, reads larger than a headcrab in the lineup (C, beside the chumtoad and roach). Clearly off or not, this is unverified, so the score is held at 1.

M3.reason: Six legs are visible (LEFT shows three per side, FRONT shows two at the sides). The teeth are not a ring: they are a scattered cluster at the front (FRONT, LEFT, BELOW). The pale belly is missing: the underside in BELOW is dark green with a few bumps, and the pale is only a stripe on the front face.

M4.reason: The body is grey-green as asked. The pale belly is not there: the pale is a front stripe and a few triangles on the top (FRONT, FRONT-LEFT), not the underside. The material reads as flat painted plastic with no wet sheen.

M5.reason: Surface detail is minimal: flat facets and no wet highlights, no markings or wear beyond the pale front stripe. The brief's wet, sludgy surface is not conveyed.

M6.reason: In the lineup (C, beside the chumtoad, roach and houndeye) the model is flat-shaded and plain, with no skin or texture detail, so a player would likely notice it is not one of the game's. Not a clear fail, since the game's own simple models are not heavily textured either.

M7.reason: It stands upright on its six legs, with the teeth at the front end (LEFT, FRONT) and the legs under the body; nothing sticks through the floor or floats.

M8.reason: checkErrors is empty and 660 triangles is well under twice what a headcrab-sized prop usually has. The median for Half-Life's own kind was not supplied, so this rests on the empty check and the count, not a direct comparison.

C1.reason: The run (run.png, WALK frames) keeps the body and legs together. In the attack (attack.png, JUMP frames 9, 13, 17, 21, 26) the teeth appear to hang off the front of the body with a visible gap, and in frames 17 and 21 sit above the body edge, so they look like they come apart from the head.

C2.reason: The contract measure (compareContract) reports that it keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts. Nothing in the pictures contradicts that.
